Given data:
- Primary voltage $V_1 = 230\text{ V}$, $50\text{ Hz}$
- Transformer ratio $= 5:1$ step-down
- Load resistance $R_L = 500\text{ }\Omega$
- Diodes are ideal ($V_{D} = 0\text{ V}$)

**Step 0: Secondary Voltage ($V_s$)**
$$\frac{V_1}{V_s} = \frac{5}{1} \implies V_s = \frac{230}{5} = 46\text{ V (rms)}$$
Peak secondary voltage ($V_m$):
$$V_m = V_s \times \sqrt{2} = 46 \times 1.414 = 65.04\text{ V}$$

**(i) D.C. Output Voltage ($V_{dc}$)**
For a bridge rectifier:
$$V_{dc} = \frac{2V_m}{\pi} = \frac{2 \times 65.04}{3.1416} = 41.4\text{ V}$$

**(ii) D.C. Power at load ($P_{dc}$)**
$$I_{dc} = \frac{V_{dc}}{R_L} = \frac{41.4\text{ V}}{500\text{ }\Omega} = 0.0828\text{ A}$$
$$P_{dc} = I_{dc}^2 \times R_L = (0.0828)^2 \times 500 = 3.43\text{ W}$$

**(iii) Peak Inverse Voltage (PIV) of each diode**
For a bridge rectifier, the PIV across each diode is equal to the peak secondary voltage:
$$\text{PIV} = V_m = 65.04\text{ V}$$

**(iv) Output frequency ($f_o$)**
For a bridge rectifier, the output frequency is double the input frequency:
$$f_o = 2 \times f_{in} = 2 \times 50\text{ Hz} = 100\text{ Hz}$$
proTip: Remember that a bridge rectifier has a PIV equal to $V_m$, whereas a center-tapped full-wave rectifier has a PIV of $2V_m$.
